Use inline captions & cross-references in Google Docs

You can insert inline captions, cross-references, and tables of captions to organize, link, and index visuals (figures, charts, tables, images, or equations) in Google Docs documents like academic papers, reports, and technical documentation.

Add an inline caption

You can insert inline captions, which act like labels to your visuals, with or without sequential numbering to figures, charts, tables, images, or equations across your document.

  • Open a document in Google Docs.
  • Select a figure, chart, table, image, or equation.
  • At the top, click Insert Page elements Inline caption .
  • On the right, in the “Inline Caption” section you can:
    • Enter caption text.
    • Select a caption type: Figure, Table, Equation, or Add custom label.
    • To add the caption type in the caption check Include label in the caption.
    • Select the numbering style.
  • Select Insert.

Insert a cross-reference

You can create text that links to the caption of a visual element and allows you to navigate directly to it. Unlike traditional links which have static display text, these cross-references can dynamically update their display text based on the caption.

Important: You must insert at least one caption in the document before you can add a cross-reference,

  • Open a document in Google Docs.
  • Place your cursor where you want the reference link to appear.
  • At the top, click Insert Page elements Cross reference Insert cross reference .
  • On the right, in the “Add cross reference” section:
    • Select a reference type, such as Figure, Table, Equation, or a custom label.
    • In the drop down menu, select from the list of the captions in your document, the caption to link to.
    • Select a display format.
  • Click Insert. Update cross-references

If you update a caption of a visual element, you can refresh to update the link.

  • To update one: Click on the linked text click Refresh cross-reference .
  • To update all references at once: Click Insert Page elements Cross reference Refresh all .

Create & manage a table of captions

Generate a structured list that details every captioned element alongside its exact document location.

  • Open a document in Google Docs.

  • Place your cursor where you want to insert the table of captions.

  • At the top, click Insert Page elements Table of captions.

  • On the right, in the “Table of Captions” section:

    • Select a “Caption label type” .
    • To add the label name and numbers in the caption check: “Include label and numbers”.

  • Select Insert. Update, edit or delete to a table of captions

  • To update a table after modifying your document: Select the table click Update table of captions .

  • To delete a table: Select the table click Delete table of captions.

  • To adjust the layout Select the table click Edit table of captions. Tip: If your table of captions is not displaying numbers: Pageless format hides page numbers and dot or dash separators in a table of captions. To display page numbers and line separators, switch your document to Pages format.

Related resources

  • Add a title, heading, or table of contents in a document.
  • Add citations and a bibliography.
  • Link a chart, table, or slides to Google Docs or Slides.

Use line numbers in Google Docs

The line numbers feature in Google Docs automatically calculates and displays the line position for a chosen portion of a document. The calculated line numbers show next to each line where the feature is turned on.

  • Improve readability and navigation: Line numbers make it easier for users to reference specific lines in their documents, specifically for long or complex documents.
  • Enhance collaboration: To provide a clear and consistent way to reference specific lines in a document, line numbers help multiple users to collaborate on a document. Important: This feature isn’t available in documents that are in pageless format. If your document includes line numbers and you switch it to a pageless format, you won’t see the line numbers . To use line numbers, make sure your document is in pages format.

Show line numbers in a document

  • To show line numbers in a document, users with edit access can accept suggestions.
  • To find line numbers, click Tools Line numbers.
  • In the line numbers sidebar, select Show line numbers.
  • By default, line numbers show and increase throughout the entire document.

Restart line numbers for new pages or sections

  • You can restart line numbers for each page or section in a document.
  • To restart line numbers, click Tools Line numbers. Then, select an option.
  • Select an option:
    • Continue throughout the document
    • Restart on each page
    • Restart on each section
  • Select where to apply to:
    • Entire document
    • This section

Show line numbers per section

  • Users can show or hide line numbers for specific portions of a document.
    • If the document doesn’t have a section, the option “This section” under “Apply to” will be disabled.
  • To create sections, insert a section break:
    • Click Insert Break Section break (next page or continuous).
  • From the line numbers sidebar, under “Apply to,” select Show line numbers and This section. Tip: To show section breaks, click View Show non-printing characters.

View document outlines, summaries, rulers, & non-printing characters

View and edit Markdown (.md) files in Google Docs

Markdown (.md or .markdown) files are a standard text format widely used by Large Language Models (LLMs) to preserve structured data.

In Google Drive and Google Docs you can:

  • Access fully ready, formatted Markdown files.
  • Open and change .md files in Google Docs without changing the file type. They stay .md files.
  • Work with others right away using comments, sharing, and working on the same file.

Preview an .md file in Drive

  • Open Google Drive and right-click your file.
  • Select Open with Preview .
  • At the top of the viewer, you can switch between Markdown and Preview.
  • To edit the file, open it in Google Docs.

Open and edit an .md file in Docs

Important: Your file does not convert to a Google Docs file. It stays an .md file, kept in Drive. Google Docs is an editor where you can see the final format and work with others.

  • Upload your .md file to Google Drive.
  • Click the .md file twice to open it in Google Docs.
    • It opens in Markdown Mode, you’ll find an .md tag next to the title . Tip: To convert an .md file into a Google Doc file, you need to use a computer and select File Save as Google Docs.
Google Docs formatting not supported in Markdown files

Some Google Docs features might change when you edit an .MD file. To restore the original click File Version history.

  • Smart chips change to text or links
  • Web formatting (.HTML) turns into plain text
  • Font colors, highlights, and text alignment are removed.

Share and collaborate on Markdown files

You can share .md files from Google Docs with your collaborators. You can add your comments and formatting when you reopen your document in Google Docs or in other tools.

You can work with collaborators in real time on Markdown files:

  • See changes as others make them.
  • Add comments to add feedback on specific text.
  • Tag people directly in comments.
  • Track changes and restore previous versions of your file. To convert an .md file into a Google Doc file, you need to use a computer and select File Save as Google Docs.

Write & edit with Gemini in Docs (Miscellaneous)

Feature availability

  • This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. Learn how to get started with Google Workspace with Gemini.

  • Learn about supported languages for Google Workspace with Gemini.

  • Google Workspace Experiments, which is a trusted tester program for personal accounts to try new AI features. Learn more about Workspace Experiments. You can draft and refine content in Google Docs using information directly from your files in Drive, Chat, Gmail, and the web.

  • Edit with a prompt: Make the introduction more concise and professional.

  • Refine with quick actions: Highlight text to Rephrase, Shorten, Elaborate, Bulletize, or Summarize the content. You can also update the content to More formal or More casual.

  • Edit using context from another file: You can use your own documents as a source to add data, evidence, and citations.

  • Use the writing style of an existing file: Gemini can edit your document’s style mirroring the writing style of existing documents.

Write, edit, or refine text with Gemini

To edit with Gemini, click Gemini . Then, enter a prompt. When you edit, you don’t need to select any text since Gemini can understand the context of your doc and make broad or specific updates based on your instructions.

  • On your computer, open a document in Google Docs.
  • To target a specific section, at the bottom bar, mention the section in the prompt. For example: “Add evidence to my Research section.”
    • Or, to refine the whole document, you can enter a prompt like “Suggest places where I can better defend my argument.”
  • Optional: Add sources for Gemini to reference when you write. Learn how to reference other files to create content.
  • Gemini will show suggestions directly in your document.
    • To apply changes individually, click Accept suggestion .
    • To apply all changes, click Accept all.
    • To reject all changes, click Reject all. Learn how to find & manage your Gemini in Workspace conversation history.

Edit text with one click

  • On your computer, open a document in Google Docs.
  • Select the text you want to rewrite.
  • On the floating bar, click Refine .
    • To refine the content, use the suggested text after you click:
      • Rephrase
      • Shorten
      • More Elaborate, More formal, More casual, Bulletize, or Summarize
  • Review the suggested changes.
    • To apply changes individually, click Accept suggestion .
    • To apply the changes, click Accept all.
    • To reject the changes, click Reject all.

Reference other files to create content

You can ask Gemini to use specific files to write, edit, or refine content. For example: “Update the project timeline based on the latest updates from our meeting notes doc.”

  • At the bottom bar, click Sources Add from Drive or other location.
    • Or, you can type “@” and then search and select from the menu.
  • Select one or more files.
  • Click Add.
Select where Gemini can search for information

You can select the locations where Gemini can proactively search for content related to your prompt. Learn how to use sources with Google Workspace with Gemini.

Examples of how you can use Gemini in Docs to write and refine your content

Your goal

You should use

Update a project status

“Update the timeline in this document based on the latest project email from yesterday.”

Change document structure

“Convert the bulleted list in the ‘To do’ section into a three-column table.”

Incorporate external data

“Add a section about our Q3 goals using information from the ‘Annual Strategy’ file in my Drive.”

Summarize a long document

Click Refine More Summarize.

Change the document formatting

“Make all the headers use the font Inter, 24pt, bold, in navy blue.”

Improve your document

“Act as a sophisticated Director of Product Management and suggest ways I can improve this doc.”

Match a different writing style

Important: This feature is available through Workspace Experiments (a trusted tester program for personal accounts.) Learn more about Workspace Experiments.

You can reference a writing style like the tone of voice, sentence structure, and vocabulary complexity from a Google Drive document.

  • On a Google Doc, on the bottom bar, click Tools .
  • Select Writing style Add a document from Drive.
  • In the pop up, click Add document.
  • Select the file you want to use. For example: You are an engineer, and your document is a technical design document and you want to reference a newsletter from the marketing team to adopt their writing style.
  • Click Add.
    • Gemini generates a summary of the writing style it applies. For example: “Formal, objective, and direct. Concise phrasing but avoid acronyms.”
  • Click Confirm.
  • Optional: If the style described doesn’t meet your preference, select a different file. Tip: If you copy and paste content to an existing document, to match its writing style, select Match writing style.

Minimize or hide the bottom bar

By default, the Gemini bar automatically minimizes to clear your screen and help you focus on what you write.

To show the Gemini bar again, at the bottom, hover over Gemini .

Move bottom bar to side panel

To keep Gemini open while you work, you can move the bottom bar to the side panel. It provides a larger response display for improved readability.

  • On your computer, open a document in Google Docs.
  • At the bottom bar, enter your prompt. For example:
    • “Generate FAQs based on recent email conversations”
    • “Add a table listing actions items and next steps”
    • “Generate an email summarizing this document so that I can share it with executive shareholders via email”
    • “Change all of the heading to blue color”
  • Click Send action .
  • At the bottom bar, click Switch to side panel .
  • Optional: To switch back, at the top of the side panel, click Switch to bottom bar .
